newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine coconut oil prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Philippine coconut oil prices seen rising.

text.p: Philippine coconut oil prices are expected to continue to rise because of delayed copra harvests, traders said on Friday.
"Local millers are on the buy side and that can only show that there is tightening supply. This will lead to a steady rise in the price of coconut oil," said one trader.
Persistent rains for the past two weeks in copra-rich Mindanao in the southern Philippines have delayed the harvest, traders added.
One trader said coconut oil prices may increase by $10 per tonne next week. He said prices have risen by as much as $20 per tonne since reports of the delayed harvest began emerging.
"As long as we don't see supply coming, prices will not likely soften in the near term," the trader said.
The trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines Inc said coconut oil was last traded at an average rate of $743.33 per tonne CIF for September/October and $733.75 for October/November.
Last month, traders projected a softening in prices of coconut oil on prospects of increase in coconut production. Historically, production reaches its peak by October.
